en.title: Ukraine seeks EU support to exclude Russian athletes from sport
en.dek: Kyiv lobbies EU ministers to maintain restrictions on Russian athletes in global tournaments
facts: Ukrainian Minister Matvii Bidnyi met EU sports ministers in Brussels on November 20
Ukraine seeks EU application of a visa ban on Moscow’s combatants to soldiers on national teams
The European Commission proposed barring Russian teams and athletes from competing in the EU
International Olympic Committee President Kirsty Coventry stated athletes should not pay for governmental actions
body: Kyiv is increasing its effort to keep Russian athletes out of global sports tournaments according to Politico Europe
Bidnyi stated he presented three demands to EU sports ministers: a ban on Russian symbols, verified neutral athlete status, and funding cuts for federations allowing Russian competition
Almost all of the 27 EU countries reportedly expressed willingness to make the exclusion a common position according to Bidnyi
Seven EU countries wrote to European Council President António Costa and Commission President Ursula von der Leyen requesting tougher visa rules on Russian nationals
The European Commission's sanctions package, which restricts financial flows from Russian sponsors, requires approval from all 27 member countries
President Volodymyr Zelensky suggested the Miami summit could allow trilateral negotiations involving Ukraine, the US, and Russia according to The Kyiv Post
en.context: The dispute over Russian participation in world sport involves differing views on governmental actions and international rules; the International Olympic Committee has eased some restrictions instituted in 2022 after the Kremlin’s full-scale invasion began according to Politico Europe
